lead: Valencia’s maritime balcony. A former port reinvented, where avant-garde architecture, sailing, gastronomy and culture meet on the Mediterranean seafront.

La Marina de Valencia is the result of an extraordinary transformation: a former commercial port turned into the largest leisure, culture and nautical space on the Mediterranean seafront in Spain. It all began when Valencia was chosen as host of the 32nd America’s Cup sailing race in 2007 — the first time this competition, more than 150 years old, was held in Europe —, which drove a complete renewal of the port infrastructure.

Today La Marina combines the avant-garde architecture of the Veles e Vents with the historic heritage of the Tinglados and the Clock Building, more than 15 restaurants with sea views, around 40 water-sports companies and a cultural calendar that includes festivals, concerts and exhibitions all year round. Access is completely free.

items.title: Veles e Vents
items.subtitle: David Chipperfield and Fermín Vázquez · America’s Cup 2007 · 10,000 m²
items.body: The most emblematic building of La Marina de Valencia and one of the city’s contemporary icons. Designed by the architects David Chipperfield — Pritzker Architecture Prize winner — and Fermín Vázquez for the 32nd America’s Cup in 2007, its minimalist structure of white steel and glass forms stepped horizontal platforms that project out over the sea. The design was conceived so that the terraces shade one another, letting you enjoy the Mediterranean without squinting. Its name comes from a 15th-century poem by Ausiàs March that tells of a journey from Italy to Valencia for love.

items.title: La Base and the Tinglados
items.subtitle: Restored 20th-century warehouses · Entrepreneurship and creativity
items.body: The Tinglados are the historic structures that housed the commercial activity of the port of Valencia during the 20th century. Their façade is decorated with paintings of fruit such as oranges and grapes, a symbol of Valencian agricultural export. Restored as cultural spaces, they now host festivals, concerts, fairs and exhibitions. La Base, the former headquarters of the Alinghi team that won the America’s Cup, is currently an innovation and entrepreneurship hub that brings together startups, training centres and the Valencia World Centre for Sustainable Urban Food.

items.title: Clock Building and the Reales Atarazanas
items.subtitle: Modernist lighthouse of the port · Witness to Valencia’s maritime history
items.body: The Clock Building is one of the architectural heritage landmarks of La Marina, a silent witness to the passing of time and the evolution of the port. Its Modernist clock tower is one of the most photographed features of the area. The Reales Atarazanas del Grao, in civil Gothic style, are one of the best-preserved historic buildings on Valencia’s seafront, a testament to the importance the city had as a Mediterranean naval power in the Middle Ages. A walk around La Marina is a tour through the architecture of three centuries.
facts: Modernist architecture · Currently used by the Port Authority

items.kicker: Sport and leisure · More than 40 companies
items.title: Water Activities · The Municipal Sailing School
items.subtitle: Sailing · Kayak · Paddle surf · Diving · Boat trips · SUP Yoga
items.body: La Marina de Valencia is the epicentre of the city’s water sports. The Municipal Sailing School offers courses for all ages and levels all year round. Around 40 specialised companies offer a very complete range of activities at sea: sailing, kayak, paddle surf, kite surf, diving, rowing, jet skis, banana boat, Ocean Pilates, SUP Yoga and canoeing. For those who prefer to sail without playing sport, there are also boat trips with meals on board, sunset excursions or night outings. The training ship Juan Sebastián de Elcano, moored in the north basin, organises visits and ocean-sailing courses.

items.title: Food and Tardeo on the Mediterranean
items.subtitle: More than 15 restaurants · Tardeo · Mediterranean rice dishes · Sunset cocktails
items.body: La Marina de Valencia is home to more than 15 restaurants with Mediterranean views, from the haute cuisine of Restaurante La Sucursal in the Veles e Vents — with two Repsol Suns — to beach bars and rice restaurants along the beachfront. The “tardeo” trend — an afternoon with drinks, nibbles and live music facing the sea — is especially popular here: the Marina Beach Club is one of the benchmark venues, with a restaurant, cocktail bar and open-air dance floor. The terraces of the Veles e Vents and Bar Malabar are perfect for an aperitif. The sunset over the Mediterranean from any of these terraces is one of the best shots in Valencia.

blocks.title: Tips for visiting La Marina
items: Tardeo (afternoon + drinks + music) is the most Valencian way to enjoy La Marina: from 17:00 to 21:00 in summer
The Veles e Vents terraces are ideal for an aperitif: arrive before 14:00 at weekends
For water activities book ahead, especially in summer: many companies sell out at weekends
The sunset from La Marina with the moored boats is one of the best shots in Valencia: arrive 30 min early
Go by metro or bike: parking can be tricky in summer. The L5–L6 line drops you at the door
The Municipal Sailing School offers courses from children to adults: check the calendar at lamarinadevalencia.com
